summary: Shivaram Dattatray Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Shankashastri Marulkar, and Maheshwarshastri Joshi. He served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1968) and headed Deccan College's Sanskrit Dictionary Department (~1987–1993).

Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1975–1984) and under Jikido Takasaki in 1988, later serving as Professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University (~1992–2002).
Shlomo Pines worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University (~1925–1926) and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1952–1977).
Shobha Rani Dash is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held a research appointment at Ryukoku University in 2010 and has served as a lecturer at Otani University.

Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and under Gadjin Nagao, Eshō Mikogami, and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University until 2003.
Shodo Yamagami specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1961–1966) and served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1969–2010).
Shogo Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University (~1971–1982). He later served as a professor at Toyo University (~2005–2010).

Shohaku Okumura works in Buddhist studies, having studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kosho Uchiyama (1972–1975). He was interim head teacher at Minnesota Zen Meditation Center (1993–1996) and director at Soto Zen Buddhism International Center in 1997.

Shoji Mori specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Toyo University (~1961–1971) and under Giyu Nishi. In 1995 he was a researcher at the Okura Institute and later an assistant professor at Toyo University (1995–2007).
Shoju Inaba was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University (~1957–1981) and held a part-time lecturer post at Nagoya University.

Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1959). He held positions at Otani University (~1965–1978), Komazawa University as an assistant professor, and Ueno Gakuen University (~1978–2002).
Shoko Miyabayashi specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1951–1958) and later held a post there (~1980–2003).
Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1929–1935). He later held a post there (~1950–1981), becoming professor emeritus.

Shoko Watanabe was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) and under Ernst Leumann. He held posts at Kyushu University (~1942–1946), Taisho University (~1947–1952), and Toyo University (~1953–1974).

Shoku Bando is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. He held posts at Fukui Prefectural College, Kyoto University, and the Abhidharma Kenkyūjo.
Shoren Ihara worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held positions as an assistant professor at Kyushu University and as a member at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Shoryu Katsura works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, having studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held posts at Hiroshima University (1976–2004), UC Berkeley (1985), and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, Horyu-ji, and under Susumu Yamaguchi. His academic posts included Otani University (1942–1952), Doho University (1948–1975), and Otani University Junior College (1952–1962).

Shoshin Ichishima was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Dean of Academic Affairs at Taisho University. He also held posts at the Tendai Mission of Hawaii (1974), the University of Hawaii as a visiting lecturer, and Sange Gakkai.

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1965) and served as an assistant professor there (~1973–2001).
